newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Reuters Poll Trend for Australia - Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Reuters Poll Trend for Australia - Dec 20.

text.p: The Australian Liberal-National government is ending the year with a far greater lead than the one that handed it a landslide election victory in March, the Reuters Poll Trend shows.
Government primary-vote support is about 13 percentage points ahead of the Labor opposition's, compared with the 8.5-point gap on election day.
There have been two honeymoons since the election.
The first and strongest took the government to an enormous 18-point lead in May. That faded until the August budget, which was followed by a second surge, peaking at around 15 points.

Prime Minister John Howard's standing as preferred prime minister has followed a similar pattern. Kim Beazley's position has barely improved in this respect since the day he took over as opposition leader after the election.
This data is an estimate for early December. Only Newspoll data is available for mid-December, trend estimates for which will be calculated when more polls are published.
